messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PD alert fired: PD-INC-4729 — embeddings-service error-rate spike (eu-west). Severity: high. Trigger: 5xx ratio > 5% for 3m. Link: https://pd.example/PD-INC-4729 runbook: /runbooks/embeddings-backend

pagerbot: auto-claim attempted. No auto-ack matched. Paging oncall (rotation: alex).

alex: acked. I'm on it. Quick status: hitting 502/504 from edge -> upstream model host pool.

raj: looking at logs now, past 2m shows connection timeouts to kvcache nodes behind the router. sample:```
[2026-03-12T15:02:23Z] router-4 - upstream=kv-cache-12 connect_timeout=3.01s err=EOF
[2026-03-12T15:02:47Z] router-1 - upstream=kv-cache-07 err=connection reset by peer
```

alex: thx. Can you confirm if it's kvcache or model-hosts? I see increased latency from kvcache latency metrics.

raj: initial check: model hosts (gpu pool) are healthy in pod status, but kvcache error rate and high p99 connect times. Might be network flapping in eu-west-1. Running quick curl check to health endpoints.

raj:```
curl -sS https://kvcache-eu-west-1.health/ready -w "%{http_code} %{time_connect}s\n" -o /dev/null
```
result: `000 3.02s` on a couple nodes.

alex: OK. Mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic for embeddings route to fallback region (eu-central) via routing policy 2) scale up dedicated kvcache instances in eu-west 3) notify CS about potential customer impact. Who can kick the routing change?

maria: I can do the routing flip. Prep checklist: ensure eu-central capacity is available and model variant compatibility ok. Will validate model variants now.

ops-lead: pinging infra team — @raj, if you can gather the node IDs with highest error, they'll look at NICs. Also please tag any capacity autoscaler events.

raj: grabbing node IDs and recent events.```
node-errors: [kvcache-07, kvcache-12, kvcache-15]\nrecent-evts: autoscaler triggered scaleDown at 14:58 -> scaleUp at 15:00 (cooldown overlap?)\n```

alex: interesting. autoscaler churn could explain transient connect timeouts. For immediate customer-facing impact: embed requests are hitting retries and latency spikes; some customers see 5xx on the API but retries reduce visible failures. Estimated affected customers: small subset (~2% of active embed requests).

tess: CS on standby. If we flip routing, what messaging should we send? I suggest: "We're routing embedding requests to eu-central to mitigate transient connectivity issues in eu-west; no data loss expected; some requests may see slightly higher latency."

alex: agree. maria, proceed with routing flip when ready. I'll keep holding the PD.

maria: initiating routing change now. Command:```
rbctl route update --service embeddings --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --strategy gradual --steps 25,50,100 --ttl 60s
```

pagerbot: routing-change job queued. Job ID: rc-20260312-31. Watch logs: https://ops-logs/rc-20260312-31

raj: watching kvcache metrics — after the first 25% step we see error-rate drop 40% on eu-west replicas that were healthy, but the bad nodes still show issues.

alex: good sign. continue. Anyone want to run a quick canary embed against eu-central to validate response shape?

maria: canary done: payloads return expected vector dims and tokenization stable. latency up ~50ms median, fine for now.

ops-lead: CS, go ahead and send the short customer note. Use internal template: INCIDENT_PAGED_MINIMAL.

[tess posts customer note in #customer-notifications] :thumbsup:

alex: monitoring. PD: leaving note: "Acked by alex. Routing flip to eu-central initiated. Mitigating via routing + scaling. Tracking oncall until full recovery."

pagerbot: PD note posted and timeline updated.

raj: pulled NIC metrics from problematic kvcache hosts — spikes correlate with cloud provider maintenance window starting 14:55 UTC. Raising ticket with cloud NIC team (ticket: CLD-7854).

maria: scaling eu-west kvcache pool by +3 instances now.`rbctl scale kvcache --region eu-west-1 --add 3`

alex: at T+12m since flip started: aggregate 5xx ratio down to 0.8% and request latency returning to normal. PD auto-escalation window cleared.

ops-lead: great. next steps: 1) follow up with cloud NIC team CLD-7854 2) postmortem draft with timeline and autoscaler tuning 3) consider lowering autoscaler aggressiveness around maintenance windows.

maria: starting runbook ticket and will coordinate with cloud support.

tess: CS: customers notified, no escalations yet. Will reopen if any reply.

alex: closing PD when steady for 30m and no error regressions. I'll hand over to next shift: @maria you'll take ownership for follow-ups if I go offline.

maria: noted, taking handoff. :handshake:

incident-bot: PD alert resolved (PD-INC-4729) — alert cleared after routing change and scale-up. Duration: ~18m.

alex: closing thread. Follow-up items logged: CLD-7854, PM-embeddings-autoscaler, postmortem draft. Thanks all. :heart:
